text:
laura-support: Hey team, customer trying to run the air-gapped installer in a heavily restricted VPC. Installer fails during the bootstrap with 403/TLS errors when pulling model images and when contacting telemetry/auth. Need a minimal egress allowlist for bootstrap only. Logs below. :grimacing:

laura-support: ```
2026-02-12T10:02:14Z installer: failed to pull registry.redwood.ai/model-shard:403 
Caused by: TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: internal error
Next: failed to contact https://telemetry.redwood.ai/collect: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

alice-se: Thanks — can you confirm this is an airgapped bootstrap (no initial container images pre-seeded)? If yes, minimal set is small but needs both package + registry + auth endpoints. Also: do they use a corporate TLS intercept (MITM) or legit CA chain?

laura-support: No pre-seeded images. Customer says corp proxy with TLS intercept is in place. They can add hosts but will not disable intercept.

sam-ops: Ok. With TLS intercept you'll need to either import the corporate CA into installer runtime or allow direct TLS passthrough for our endpoints. If passthrough not possible, list below is the minimum hostnames the installer tries to reach during bootstrap (TLS 443):
- registry.redwood.ai
- artifacts.redwood.ai (pip/wheels/artifactory)
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai (token exchange / model auth)
- kms.redwood.ai (for key provisioning if they opted in)
- model-shards.redwood.ai (shard CDN / S3-backed endpoints)

sam-ops: Ports: 443 outbound. DNS must resolve to public IPs; split-horizon can break cert/SNI.

antony: Also add: gcr.io / docker.pkg.redwood (if they pull any base images from public registries) and pypi.org + files.pythonhosted.org for pip bootstrapping. If customer vendors mirror these internally, point installer at mirror, but default installer expects public endpoints.

laura-support: Customer specifically asked for a compact allowlist they can present to security. Can we provide a one-page hostlist + optional CIDR ranges?

alice-se: Yes. Short version (text they can paste into a firewall):
- registry.redwood.ai:443
- artifacts.redwood.ai:443
- telemetry.redwood.ai:443
- auth.redwood.ai:443
- kms.redwood.ai:443 (optional)
- model-shards.redwood.ai:443
- pypi.org:443
- files.pythonhosted.org:443
- gcr.io:443 (optional; only if using Google base images)

alice-se: Note: If their TLS intercept rewrites SNI or terminates TLS, they must either import their CA into our runtime or configure the proxy to allow CONNECT passthrough to the above hosts. If using split-horizon DNS, ensure records resolve to the same cert CNs we present (SNI matters).

infra-oncall: Quick ask: do we have IP ranges we can publish? We prefer hostnames because IPs are on CDNs and can change. But if security insists on CIDRs, recommend allowing the cloud provider ranges for our registry + the CDN provider (we'll escalate for exact CIDRs once customer confirms region).

laura-support: Customer will accept hostnames first. Security wants to know whether telemetry calls are mandatory for installer success or can be disabled during bootstrap.

antony: Telemetry calls are not strictly mandatory for image pulls, but the installer checks in for feature flags and can fail if auth handshake cannot be established. For a true bootstrap without telemetry you can run with --offline-mode but that requires pre-seeding images and skipping token provisioning. Not ideal for first-time airgapped installs.

laura-support: Got it. They want non-invasive option: allow the hostnames for initial bootstrap, then we can switch to mirror/offline for maintenance.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: I pushed a short KB draft: https://kb.redwood.ai/airgap-bootstrap-egress (internal) with the hostlist and an example firewall snippet.

alice-se: I'll paste a firewall snippet they can hand to security (curl able):

```
# Example firewall rules (allow outbound TLS)
ALLOW tcp OUT registry.redwood.ai:443
ALLOW tcp OUT artifacts.redwood.ai:443
ALLOW tcp OUT telemetry.redwood.ai:443
ALLOW tcp OUT auth.redwood.ai:443
ALLOW tcp OUT model-shards.redwood.ai:443
ALLOW tcp OUT pypi.org:443
ALLOW tcp OUT files.pythonhosted.org:443
```

antony: Also include this quick repro curl they can run from their bastion to validate TLS passthrough and SNI:

```
curl -v https://registry.redwood.ai/health -I
# Expected: 200 OK, Server header (or 302) and cert CN that includes registry.redwood.ai
```

laura-support: Customer ran a curl and saw a cert for corp-proxy.local which confirms TLS intercept. Security will either add CA to their nodes or allow passthrough for the above hosts. I'll update ticket with the hostlist + KB link and ask them which route they prefer. :eyes:

eng-sre-bot: Ticket created: SPT-8921 — Escalate to Eng SRE for potential installer CA-import guidance and region CIDRs.

laura-support: Thanks all — keeping this thread updated with customer decision. If they choose CA import we can provide the exact Java/OS/pkcs11 steps they need.
